findings.reason: without a stated minimum of same-regime pairs (and a definition of what identifies a regime), the gate the plan believes it is placing over the rewritten names can pass vacuously, so §6's non-regression claim would later rest on nothing.
findings.text: §2's revised bullet requires "its score ... recorded beside the score the same name carried before, each with the review regime that produced it", then makes the only comparison — "the median is not lower" — apply only "where both scores come from one regime", while explicitly excluding "a score that is only a pass recorded at the acceptance floor" from comparison; nothing in the plan or the review path supplies a regime identifier (no such field exists in `imas_codex/standard_names/review/`, whose records carry an acceptance cutoff and a cascade probability, not a regime name), and no minimum count of same-regime pairs is set, so a node may satisfy the bullet by reporting a median over one name, or over none, and be closed with no non-regression shown; the bullet's other half, "every name written this way passes the documentation review it is given", cannot fail on its own because a name that fails review is not stored and so is never "a name written this way"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited directory resolves and contains `published-operator-census.txt` and `published-family-census.txt`, the operator-form and per-family wording censuses the bullet relies on.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's revised score bullet (plan.html:66) makes the only non-regression measure conditional on "both scores come[ing] from one regime", a condition no review record can answer, and sets no floor on how many names that leaves.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the wording census and the gate log are committed under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-definitions-by-construction/`, which exists and holds the operator and family census scripts and their output.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2 introduces no symbol, file or test name, and states its mechanism without a ticket, stage or version label.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the mechanism §2 states is the one §1's cited census supports (a family of 18 members carrying 18 description templates), the endpoint it names is obtainable from a disposable-graph run, and the section prescribes no code path, step sequence, formula or function.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — every done-when in §2 measures one deliverable, that shared definition parts are rendered from one stored wording; the per-member cost line is a measurement of that same pass, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` (plan.html:23) gives s6 on s2–s5, s5 on s4 and s7 on s6 plus `sn-domain-per-family#s3`, and §2 needs no section dependency because the population input it names is a decision already recorded on this plan (species-population, ions-all-charge-states).
